target_customer: Migrants in North America and Europe sending money to family in Africa and elsewhere
problem: Sending money to Africa meant high fees and weak guarantees. Sendwave offered fee free transfers from a phone app, earning on the exchange rate.
business_model: Remittance FX margin with no explicit transfer fee

founders.name: Drew Durbin
founders.background_notes: Started the company after the hassle and cost of sending money to an NGO in Tanzania, per his own profile.

founders.name: Lincoln Quirk
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in funding coverage of Wave.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs mobile money integrations with African carriers and multi country compliance, moderate engineering with heavy partnership work.

defensibility.rationale: Licenses and mobile money partnerships took time, but remittance apps were copyable and competition on price was intense.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WorldRemit, a direct rival, acquired Sendwave in 2020 in a cash and stock deal.

market_need_then: Remittance fees to Africa were high; the founder's own Tanzania experience prompted the product. Specific 2014 fee data was not found.

identity.logo: A penguin until 2024, then a wave shaped S forming a globe (DesignStudio)
identity.voice_and_tone: Send money with love; as easy as sending a text

branding.brand_signature: Penguin logo, replaced in the 2024 rebrand

rebrands.why: Separate the remittance app from the Wave mobile money business

rebrands.to: Wave S globe identity by DesignStudio
rebrands.why: New identity for the Zepz era with a diaspora by the diaspora message

branding.community_and_virality: No referral or community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Trusted by over 1 million users per its site and a notable penguin identity, but evidence is the company's own claims.

outcome_analysis: Sendwave grew remittances to Africa on a no fee pitch from a Tanzania insight and was bought by rival WorldRemit in 2020, with a headline of about 500M on the YC page though CNBC calls the price undisclosed. Post merger, parent Zepz cut 26 percent of staff in 2023 to remove duplicate roles. Funding history is almost entirely unknown.
notes: YC lists batch Winter 2012 but founded 2014; other sources say Wave started 2012 or 2014, so the dates conflict. Funding: an aggregator (CB Insights) shows only 150K from Y Combinator, Partech and Serena Ventures, unverified; the 200M Series A in 2021 belongs to Wave, a separate business. The 500M sale price appears only as a YC news headline; CNBC says undisclosed. No dated competitor sources from 2014 were found, so the list is empty; a later analysis names Western Union, MoneyGram and WorldRemit. Wave name origin not found. Added a 2016-05 Series A of 9.5M from Seedtable only, a single database; the same site's 500M seed entry dated 2012-03 looks mislabeled and is not recorded. CB Insights total of 150K conflicts.
